## Description

Context: what we decided and why. In a chain a patient who visits Surat and then Mumbai is one person with one chart. Patients are one shared record across the organisation: one MRN and one chart, opened by staff at any location under the existing access, care-relationship and audit rules. Tenant isolation stays on the organisation: the EF filter and row-level security use the tenant, not the facility. Overlap: MDV-P7-002 and MDV-P7-003 (record authority per facility) deal with hospital groups; this is the clinic-level version, built first.
What to build. Check what assumes patient-per-facility and change it: Patient.FacilityId stays as where the patient was registered; PatientRegistry allocates the MRN with NextMrnAsync(tenantId, facilityId) and requires registration at the active facility, searches by facility (FacilityId filter around line 140) and checks duplicates by facility: move the MRN sequence, search and duplicate scope to the organisation. PatientDirectory.cs and PatientMerges.cs filter pairs by FacilityId (merge and review queues): scope them to the organisation. RegistrationCareRelationship.cs and AccessRequestEndpoints.cs and the care-relationship rules must still hold for staff at another location. Scheduling, Encounters and Billing references by patient stay valid. The access log shows the location where the record was read (role and facility at event time exist). Existing MRNs stay unique; migration handles two facilities of one tenant that issued the same MRN (collision plan in the ticket). Out of scope: reassigning or walking in a patient between doctors of different locations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Given a patient registered at location A, when staff at location B of the same organisation search by name, MRN or phone, then the patient is found and opens as one chart with one MRN.
- [ ] **AC2.** Given a new registration at location B, when the name and date of birth match a patient at location A, then the duplicate warning shows that patient.
- [ ] **AC3.** Given staff at location B open the record, when the access log is read, then the entry shows location B.
- [ ] **AC4.** Given staff from another organisation, when they search or open the record, then it is refused by both the EF filter and row-level security.
- [ ] **AC5.** Given a member not scoped to location B, when they search there, then they cannot reach it (MDV-P1-071).
- [ ] **AC6.** Given existing data with the same MRN at two facilities of one tenant, when the migration runs, then every MRN is unique per organisation and nothing is lost.

## Test notes

- Unit: MRN allocation per organisation, duplicate matching scope.
- Integration on real PostgreSQL: search, duplicate, merge across locations; row-level security and EF filter on tenant; migration with colliding MRNs; mutation check on the isolation.
- Playwright: register at one location, find and open at another (journey J3 variant).
- Security: ponytail-review (tenancy and consent), access log content, no PHI in logs.
- Browser: English and Arabic, axe clean.

## Definition of Done

All acceptance criteria above, **plus** the cross-cutting X1–X8 checklist in [docs/05-delivery](../../README.md#definition-of-done-every-ticket).
